decisions.reason: As a niche agriculture-specific crate with only limited website prominence after launch, its market test likely provided enough evidence by 2022 that the option value is lower than the benefit of reallocating resources to broader packaging opportunities.

A foldable large container fits the firm's core reusable logistics portfolio across several customer industries, and its stronger launch visibility suggests a still-attractive option with good upside relative to carrying cost.
A stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's standard offering and can serve many sectors, so even without standout visibility it remains a low-cost option worth keeping on the market.
A medium-duty rackable pallet is a solid adjacency to the firm's pallet business, and its broad operational fit makes it more sensible to retain than to exit despite only modest launch prominence.

The shift from a dedicated page to only a mention points to weaker traction for this more specialized spill-retention pallet, so with several other options available management would likely discontinue it.

This pallet variant remains reasonably aligned with the firm's core transport-packaging business, and because it likely leverages existing pallet capabilities its option value still slightly exceeds its carrying cost.
